Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Ravindra Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Ravindra Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajeev Sonkar, learned State
Law Officer for the State.
3.

The present application has been filed to quash the charge sheet no. 312/2015 issued on 30.06.2015 u/s 420 I.P.C. in Case Crime No. 373 of 2014, Police Station- Tundla, District- Firozabad, and also quash the proceeding of Criminal Case No. 5037 of 2015 (State Vs. Rani Devi and others).
4. Facts giving rise to the present controversy is that an F.I.R. was lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicant and four other persons u/s 420 I.P.C. with the allegation that property was purchased by the mother of opposite party no.2 on 26.06.1967 through sale deed.

sentences.text: Even her ration card as well as electricity connection was also prepared on the basis of the address of that property.

Thereafter, the aforesaid property was again transferred in favour of co-accused,
Smt. Rani and Umesh Kumar through sale deed dated 25.05.2001 and again on 17.07.2001 for remaining part.
Both the sale deeds were witnessed by the present applicant.
The police after investigation has submitted charge-sheet against all the persons including the present applicant u/s 420 I.P.C. which is under challenge.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant was the marginal witness in the sale deed dated 25.05.2001 and 17.07.2001, therefore, he has not committed any forgery.
He bonafidely signed on those sale deeds as witness.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that co-accused Smt. Rani on the basis of aforesaid sale deeds also obtained loan from the Central Bank of India.
Subsequently, that loan was also paid by Smt. Rani, therefore, at present mortgage of the house of opposite party no. 2 is not in existence.
It is further submitted that the impugned proceeding is purely civil in nature which has been given colour of criminality.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. submitted that it is not in dispute that the house in question was purchased by mother of opposite party no. 2 on 26.06.1967 which was gifted to opposite party no. 2 and name of opposite party no. 2 was duly recorded in revenue records.
Therefore, witnessing the sale deeds dated 25.05.2001 and 17.07.2001 by the applicant shows his involvement in the forgery.
Therefore, no case for interference is made out.

7. After hearing the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of record, it appears that these facts are undisputed that mother of opposite party no.2 purchased the property in question through sale deed dated 26.06.1967 on which mother of opposite party no.2 also made construction of the house and shops which was subsequently gifted to opposite party no.2 and her name was duly recorded in the revenue record as well as electricity connection and sale deed for the same property was executed by one Sobaran Singh, who was the vendee of mother of opposite party no.2, in favour of co-accused, Smt. Rani on 25.05.2001 and 17.07.2001 and both the sale deeds were witnessed by the applicant.
Therefore, at this stage, it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicant.
8. In view of the above, this Court does not find any illegality in the impugned proceedings.
9. Accordingly, the present application is dismissed.
